reading.title: Inside Grandma's Cedar Chest
reading.purpose: Join Sofia and her grandmother as they uncover family keepsakes and stories from long ago.
paras: On a wet Sunday, Sofia helped her grandma open an old cedar chest in the attic. Inside lay soft quilts, brass snaps, and a worn map held with tape.
"This map was your great-grandpa's," Grandma said. "He was an ancestor who lived long before us. As a young immigrant, he left his homeland across the sea and came here to start a new life."

Sofia traced a tiny ink dot on the map. "He lived near a small coastal settlement where folks built log homes," Grandma said. "Long before that, the town had been a colony ruled by a far king. Later, local folks formed their own government with fair rules."

Next, Grandma took out a wood spoon with flowers on it. "His sister went west to the frontier, the edge of settled land where few folks lived. Still, our kin kept our culture alive with songs, food, and tales."
"At each fall ceremony, our town meets to sing those songs," Grandma smiled. "You are a proud descendant of folks who worked hard and kept their roots."

choices: a carved wooden spoon passed down by a family
the edge of settled land where few people live
a special harvest event with songs and recipes
a town ruled by a king who lives far away
qs.why: Paragraph 4 defines the frontier as "the edge of settled land where few people lived yet."

qs.q: Which sentence tells what an ancestor is?
choices: "This map was your great-grandpa's," Grandma said.
"He was an ancestor who lived long before us.
Sofia traced a tiny ink dot on the map.
"You are a proud descendant of folks who worked hard and kept their roots."
qs.why: This sentence explains that an ancestor is a family member who lived long before you.

ev.text: "He was an ancestor who lived long before us.

qs.q: How did Sofia's family keep its culture alive after moving to new places?
choices: They shared their songs, food, and tales over the years.
They left all of their old quilts and wooden spoons behind in the attic.
They asked a far king to write new rules for their fall festival.
They stopped visiting the coastal settlement once the map faded.
qs.why: Paragraph 4 says the kin kept their culture alive with songs, food, and tales.

qs.q: What is this story mostly about?
choices: How to repair a worn paper map using clear tape and soft attic quilts
Sofia learning about her family's past from old keepsakes
Why coastal settlements always grow faster than towns on a frontier
How local leaders elect a new government during a wet Sunday meeting
qs.why: Through the items in Grandma's chest, Sofia learns about her ancestors, their moves, and the traditions she carries on.

clues.text: the edge of settled land where few folks lived
